J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "In a circuit-free graph, any walk is a path." The first-choice line 7 is "3. By def., tree is circuit-free, so P_1 is a path (since path has no repeated edges and no repeated vertices)", and the only thing known about P_1 at that point is line 6, "By def., tree is connected, so, there is a walk P_1 between u and v" - an arbitrary walk, with no minimality, shortness or non-repetition assumed. So the step's content is exactly the general implication the response states, applied to that arbitrary walk, and the line even supplies the definition of "path" that the implication needs.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: The witness names the graph family and the walk explicitly: "In a tree with an edge between u and v, the walk u-v-u-v is not a path as it repeats vertices and edges, despite the tree being circuit-free." The smallest member of the named family is determined (the tree consisting of the single edge uv), and the offending walk is written out, so nothing needed to be supplied.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Checked by direct finite verification of exactly the supplied witness (script kept). Taking T to be the tree on {u,v} with the single edge uv: T is connected and has no circuit (no cycle on three or more vertices and no parallel edges), so it is a tree and u != v, satisfying the assumptions in force at lines 5-7. The sequence u-v-u-v has every consecutive pair an edge, so it is a walk between u and v as in line 6; it repeats both a vertex and an edge, so by line 7's own definition of path it is not a path. Hence circuit-freeness does not license line 7's inference, and the line is false as written for the arbitrary walk it is applied to.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response gives three candidate lines (7, 16, 20), the claim and the counterexample, and states no consequence: it does not assert that the theorem at line 1 is false (it is true), nor that the case analysis at lines 14-28 or the conclusion at line 32 collapses. So there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: The defect is real but repairable in one word (choose P_1 to be a walk of minimum length, or a walk with no repeated vertex), so an adjudicator may want to weigh whether it is the intended target: the theorem is true and the rest of the argument is unaffected by this step. Two definitional points a second reader should confirm rather than assume: u-v-u-v counts as a walk under the usual definition (backtracking is allowed; it is a trail that is forbidden from repeating edges), and retracing one edge does not create a circuit, so the tree stays circuit-free - the author's own line 54 remark shows he is thinking about multigraphs, where a circuit would need two parallel edges.
